tagline.text: A two-tier waterfall in the Laurel hills that falls like drizzle

location.label: Location
location.text: Sitio Salipit, Barangay San Gabriel, Laurel, Batangas

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (round-trip transport from Manila and guide, per person)

children.text: Hidden deep in Barangay San Gabriel in Laurel, Batangas, this two-tier waterfall is said to be about 60 m high. Its spray drifts down like light rain, which gives the falls their name, and it pairs well with neighboring Malagaslas Falls on a half-day trek.

Ambon-Ambon Falls lies inside Sitio Salipit in Barangay San Gabriel, in the town of Laurel, Batangas. Laurel is a small town west of Taal Lake, right below the Tagaytay ridge, about 85 km from Manila. The name is said to come from the Tagalog word for drizzle, and it captures the way the water breaks into fine mist and sprinkles visitors.
Sources differ a little on the height, but many travel accounts describe
a two-tier waterfall of about 60 m

. One stream drops straight off a large boulder, while the other drifts down as a soft mist. The Laurel municipal tourism page also says the water falls in two places, and highlights the tunnel-like river path shaded by trees and the river cutting through a huge rock. The water is clear and good for swimming, but it can turn muddy when the upstream floods in the rainy season.

Most visitors see it together with Malagaslas Falls, which sits along the trail. Malagaslas is a stretch of small cascades and natural pools, a favorite picnic spot for locals, and Ambon-Ambon is a little farther in on foot. The round trip takes half a day at most, so some people combine it with a Taal Volcano trek or a Tagaytay outing on the same day.

One thing to watch for: several waterfalls share the name. Within Laurel alone there is one in San Gabriel and another in Bagong Pook, the neighboring town of Talisay has one in Barangay Miranda, and there are also Ambon-Ambons in Pangil, Laguna and Bagac, Bataan. This guide covers
the falls at Salipit in San Gabriel, Laurel
. Map apps can send you to the wrong place, so confirm the location before you set out.

blocks.title: A two-tier stream of about 60 m

children.text: One stream falls straight off a rock while another drifts down like mist, and the two meet in one spot. It is described as one of the tallest waterfalls in Laurel and in Batangas as a whole.
This fine spray gives the falls their name. Up close it feels like standing in light rain without an umbrella, a good way to cool off on a hot day.

The trail passes under overhanging trees and along a river that cuts through a large rock before reaching the falls. Laurel's tourism information also presents this stretch as the highlight of the trek.
About
10 minutes

from the start of the trail you reach Malagaslas Falls. Small cascades, pools and picnic huts make it a good place to rest. The name is said to come from the "lagaslas" sound of water hitting the rocks.
Many visitors report swimming in the cool water below the falls after the trek. Water volume and the areas open for swimming change with the season and upkeep, so follow the instructions on site.
You walk past coconut farms, small rice fields, streams and boulders. It is a pleasant glimpse of quiet Philippine village life.
The Tagaytay ridge, Taal Lake and the volcano are close, so it is easy to combine them in one day. San Gabriel also has Antona Chapel, a chapel built in a cave.
Take a bus from Manila (Buendia and elsewhere) to Tanauan or Tagaytay. One account says the first jeepney to Laurel leaves around
, so start early in the morning.
In Tanauan town, transfer to a jeepney bound for Laurel. Get off at Laurel's town hall area (poblacion) and check the entry and guide arrangements at the tourism desk or the barangay hall.
From the poblacion, take a tricycle or motorcycle taxi to the Salipit trailhead. The fare is usually around
one way, but it is negotiable and worth confirming locally.
Start walking from the trailhead. After about
10 minutes
you reach Malagaslas Falls, and after another
10~30 minutes
farther in you arrive at Ambon-Ambon. You will cross streams several times, so wear shoes that can get wet.
Take photos, swim and rest below the falls. The mist is fine and heavy, so a waterproof bag helps.
Return to Malagaslas for lunch and a rest, then head down to the trailhead before any afternoon rain.
Have a light snack in Laurel and start the trip home. Check the last jeepney and bus times beforehand.
Public transport does not run on a fixed schedule, so leave yourself plenty of time. Be sure to confirm the last departure times locally.

items.title: Overnight with Tagaytay
items.subtitle: Two days combined with the Tagaytay ridge

children.text: Have breakfast in Tagaytay and visit a viewpoint. The ridge overlooking Taal Lake and the volcano is close and sets the mood nicely.
Head down through Talisay to Laurel along Sungay Road or similar roads. Check road conditions and transport on site.
Trek from Laurel to the falls. Avoid going right after heavy rain.
Visit Antona Chapel in Laurel or a Taal Lake viewpoint, then return to Manila.
San Gabriel is said to have lodge-style stays and resort tour packages, but operations change, so confirm before booking.

Drive from Manila through SLEX and Calamba up to Tagaytay, then go down toward Talisay and Laurel via Sungay Road or similar roads. One account puts the distance from Manila to Laurel town hall at about

The roads near the trailhead are narrow and rough, so a motorcycle taxi or tricycle may be easier than a car. Ask locally where to park.

A waterfall shows its true form only when the water is plentiful. Several bloggers say the best time is one or two months after the rainy season ends, while some reviews note the flow gets weak in the height of summer.
If heavy rain fell just before your visit, the upstream floods, the water turns murky and the trail gets slippery. Avoid days with rain in the forecast and set out early in the morning.

Laurel town and the San Gabriel area have small eateries and neighborhood stores (sari-sari) for simple meals and drinks. There is almost nothing to eat near the falls, so bring water and snacks. Reviews mention a small store and huts at Malagaslas, but check on site whether they are open.

Places to stay are more plentiful in Tagaytay and Talisay than in Laurel itself. Some reviews describe using a resort on the San Gabriel foothills (with tour packages) as a base, but things change, so confirm before booking. A local specialty is tawilis, a freshwater sardine found only in Taal Lake.
Check the guide and entry arrangements first at Laurel town hall or the San Gabriel barangay hall. Tourism information warns that the winding trail can make you lose your way without a guide.
Wear sandals or water shoes that can get wet. You cross streams many times and walk on a mix of rock and mud.
Bring a waterproof bag, a change of clothes and a towel. You get wet quickly in front of the falls.
Entrance, parking and guide fees may be collected separately, so carry plenty of small change.
Starting early helps you avoid afternoon showers and see the falls when they are quiet.
Reviews say map apps may point to the wrong access road, so check the way again with a local in the poblacion.
Phone signal and battery may weaken, so download an offline map.
Right after rain the stream swells, the trail gets slippery and the water turns murky, so avoid the rainy season and days with rain in the forecast.
There are many stream crossings, and the water can rise suddenly. Plan so that you are not coming down late.
Some rocks are sharp or slippery when wet. Check the depth of the pool below the falls and do not jump from the rocks.
There is a record that the area was once inside a private estate with a required guide and package prices. Check the latest entry rules and whether access is allowed on site.
Several waterfalls share the same name, so confirm the location repeatedly to avoid going to the wrong one.
The last public transport can leave early, so decide your way home in advance.
A ridge town overlooking Taal Lake and the volcano. Head up from Laurel to enjoy viewpoints and cafes.
A historic town with Spanish-era buildings, away from Laurel on the south side of Taal Lake, so it needs a separate trip. Travel time depends on traffic.
Tiered falls on the way to Ambon-Ambon, good for picnics and a dip.
